questions.prompt: Why does `MainViewModel` take an `IDialogService` in its constructor instead of calling `MessageBox.Show("Saved")` directly?
options: `MessageBox.Show` cannot be called from inside a command's action
`IDialogService` is a built-in WPF interface that shows dialogs faster
It depends on an interface, so it stays free of UI types and testable
It lets the ViewModel open any Window by calling `Window.Show()`
questions.explanation: `IDialogService` is a custom abstraction, not built into WPF. Calling `MessageBox.Show` in a ViewModel couples it to the UI, breaks MVVM and is hard to unit test; depending on the interface avoids all three.

source.section: Want to communicate between windows? - use IDialogService Interface

questions.prompt: `InputDialogViewModel` has no reference to its Window. How does clicking OK close the dialog?
options: It raises `RequestClose`, which is wired to `window.Close()`
`Accept()` calls `Application.Current.MainWindow.Close()` directly
The OK button's `IsDefault` property closes the window automatically
The DialogService polls `DialogResult` until it is no longer `null`
questions.explanation: The ViewModel only raises `RequestClose`. When the DialogService creates the window it wires `vm.RequestClose += () => window.Close();`, so the ViewModel never touches the Window.

questions.prompt: Why must `IMessageBus` be registered with `services.AddSingleton<IMessageBus, MessageBus>()`?
options: Singletons are the only lifetime that can hold a `lock` object
So publishers and subscribers all share the same bus instance
Because `MessageBus` references WPF types such as the Dispatcher
So each ViewModel gets its own private copy of the handlers
questions.explanation: Subscribers are stored inside the bus instance. If each component got its own bus, a publisher's messages would never reach subscribers registered on a different instance.

questions.prompt: Put one successful pass of the `AutoSaveService` loop in order.
steps: Check `_tracker.HasChanges` (skip the rest if nothing changed)
Publish `new AutoSaveStatus(DateTime.Now, true, "Autosave completed")` on the bus
questions.explanation: Each pass delays, skips if the tracker is clean, saves, marks the tracker clean, then publishes an `AutoSaveStatus` that subscribers such as `MainViewModel` react to.

questions.prompt: `AutoSaveService` publishes from a background thread, and the subscriber updates `StatusText`, which is bound to the UI. If the bus calls `handler?.Invoke(message);` directly, what happens?
options: WPF automatically switches the handler over to the UI thread
The message waits in a queue until the window is next activated
Nothing goes wrong, because property changes are thread-safe
It runs on the background thread and can crash on UI-bound state
questions.explanation: Direct invocation runs on the current thread with no thread switch. WPF has thread affinity, so UI-bound state must be updated through `Dispatcher.Invoke`/`BeginInvoke`, which forces execution on the UI thread.

questions.prompt: Where should `_host.StopAsync()` be called in a WPF app that uses the Generic Host?
options: Only in `App.OnExit()`, in `App.xaml.cs`
In the main ViewModel's Close command
Inside each BackgroundService when it finishes
In the main Window's `Closing` event handler
questions.explanation: Stopping the host signals cancellation to all BackgroundServices, waits for them, flushes logs and disposes services, which is application-level work. Call it only in `App.OnExit()`, never from ViewModels, Windows or BackgroundServices.
